card.name: Adverse events to watch for
card.fires_on: The noun naming a harmful event that clinicians are told to watch for, such as "events" after "development of such" or "seizures" after "evaluate patients at frequent intervals for". It appears in monitoring warnings.

modes.label: Such events in NSAID warning
modes.description: The word "events" ending the phrase "remain alert for the development of such" in the NSAID cardiovascular warning.
modes.example: Physicians and patients should remain alert for the development of such<< events>>, throughout the entire treatment course, even

modes.label: Seizures in monitoring advice
modes.description: The word "seizures" after "evaluate patients at frequent intervals for" in opioid interaction text.
modes.example: Evaluate patients at frequent intervals for<< seizures>> and serotonin syndrome, and signs of respiratory

card.writes: It favors words meaning occurrence, like "occurred" and "occurring", which suggests the text goes on to say when the event happens.
card.plain: It fires on the named bad outcome in a "watch for this" warning, just before the text talks about it occurring.
